assistant_messages.content:
All three views are rendered above. Here's what they show:

**1. Invoice approval flow (diagram 1)** — Every supplier invoice follows the same fixed sequence: it's received and logged in the payables register the same working day, then put through a three-way match against the purchase order and goods receipt note [3]. Matched invoices go to the budget holder (5 working days), invoices over €10,000 also need finance controller sign-off, and approved invoices are scheduled for the weekly run [1]. Treasury releases payment on the Thursday run, and the invoice, PO and approvals are archived for seven years [4]. The two side paths: mismatches are returned to the supplier — a rejected invoice is never paid — and resubmissions re-enter the match step [1]; and if the budget holder hasn't approved after reminders, the invoice escalates to the Head of Finance [2]. One governance rule worth noting: nobody may approve an invoice they raised themselves [2].

**2. Atlas vs Borealis (comparison 1)** — The contracts diverge meaningfully on all three dimensions. Borealis is the more flexible to exit: 30 days' convenience notice versus Atlas's 90 [5] [10]. Their "for cause" triggers differ — Atlas covers uncured material breach, Borealis covers insolvency [5] [10]. Liability is structured differently too: Atlas caps each party at 12 months' fees with four carve-outs (death, personal injury, fraud, confidentiality), while Borealis carries a hard €250,000/year cap on its side with only fraud excluded [5] [10]. On renewal, Atlas auto-renews annually with a 90-day notice window, whereas the Borealis MSA is a fixed two-year term with no renewal clause — and that term ran from 1 June 2024, so it has already expired (31 May 2026) [5] [10].

**3. Atlas timeline (timeline 1)** — The history runs from signature on 14 March 2023 [11] through Amendment 1 (Feb 2024), a November 2024 SLA breach notice that led to €18,400 in service credits, and the April 2026 price uplift of 3.1% [11]. The two live dates: **15 December 2026** — the non-renewal notice deadline, roughly seven weeks from today — and **15 March 2027**, when the current term ends and auto-renews for a year unless notice was given [6]. If you're weighing the SLA history against renewal, that notice date is the decision point.

One caveat: all three documents are marked as generated UAT fixtures ("no real supplier, person or amount"), so treat the specifics as test data rather than live commercial terms [3] [5] [10].
